We need a retrosynthesis route with max 1 step (i.e., a single reaction) from commercially available precursors, total price <= $125. Need to propose route. The target is methyl ester of a carboxylic acid? SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. That's methyl 3-(trimethylsilyl)phenyl acrylate? Actually structure: methyl ester of a cinnamic acid derivative with a TMS group on phenyl? The core: COC(=O)-C(=C)-c1ccc... plus TMS on phenyl? The SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. So methyl ester attached to a carbon bearing a cyclopropyl? Wait C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclopropyl? Actually C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclopropene? Not sure. But we have a carbonyl carbon attached to OCH3 and to a carbon that is attached to a cyclopropyl with TMS? Might be a methyl ester of a cyclopropyl-substituted cinnamate.

We have template 38636 which seems to be esterification: product is ester, reactants are carboxylic acid (O-[C]... ) and alcohol (C-OH). The retro template: product (ester) -> carboxylic acid + alcohol. So we can propose retrosynthesis: break ester into corresponding acid and methanol. The acid would be O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]-[C:4]=[C:5] which corresponds to the acid: O=C(O)-C(=C)-aryl? Actually acid SMILES: O=C(O)C(=C)C6=... plus TMS? The acid would be O=C(O)C(=C)C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2? Wait the acid is same as target but with OH instead of OCH3. So acid SMILES: O=C(O)C(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2). That's not exactly but we can generate.

Thus route: target ester from methanol and corresponding acid. Both need to be commercially available. Methanol is cheap. The acid maybe not commercially available. Could we use alternative: use acyl chloride and methanol? Template may also allow acid chloride + methanol. But we need commercially available precursors. Maybe we can get the acid (cinnamic acid derivative) commercially? Search for that acid. Let's try search catalog for acid SMILES: O=C(O)C(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2).
